inputs.name: ticks

inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

device.name: LeRobot MuJoCo tutorial OMY robot scene

facts.text: The README title is 'LeRobot Tutorial with MuJoCo' and it describes minimal examples for collecting demonstration data and training vision-language-action models on custom datasets.
The README tells the user to install the requirements with mujoco version 3.1.6.
The README tells the user to unzip asset/objaverse/plate_11.zip before use.
The served scene is the MJCF model 'open_manipulator_y scene' and it includes omy.xml.
The robot model compiles angles in radians with autolimits enabled and sets the implicitfast integrator.
Default class Y declares joint range -6.28319 to 6.28319, armature 0.1 and damping 100.0.
Default class Y's position actuator has kp 5000, forcerange -2000 to 2000 and ctrlrange -6.28319 to 6.28319.
The arm is a six-joint chain joint1 through joint6, all of default class Y.
The gripper has four joints: rh_r1 and rh_l1 have range 0 to 1.1 and rh_r2 and rh_l2 have range 0 to 1, all of default class gripper.
Default class gripper's position actuator has kp 1000 and forcerange -100 to 100 but no ctrlrange.
The model has ten position actuators: six arm actuators of class Y (actuator_joint1 through actuator_joint6) and four gripper actuators that declare ctrlrange 0 to 1.1, 0 to 1, 0 to 1.1 and 0 to 1.
The robot model declares a camera named egocentric.
The served scene's worldbody contains a floor plane and a directional light.
The card's entry symbol SimpleEnv is a concrete class in mujoco_env/y_env.py that constructs MuJoCoParserClass from the xml_path argument.
SimpleEnv.step for joint_angle takes action[:-1] as the six joint targets, repeats action[-1] four times for the gripper command and scales elements 1 and 3 by 0.8.
SimpleEnv.step stores self.q and returns the selected state; SimpleEnv.step_env separately calls self.env.step(self.q).
SimpleEnv.get_joint_state returns the six joint angles plus a binary gripper state.
SimpleEnv.grab_image reads the agentview, egocentric and sideview camera frames.
The card's second entry symbol SimpleEnv2 is a concrete class in mujoco_env/y_env2.py.
SimpleEnv2.set_instruction chooses the red mug body_obj_mug_5 or the blue mug body_obj_mug_6 from the instruction.
The tutorial's example scene includes the tabletop, mug_5 and plate_11 object models in addition to the OMY robot model.

determinism.notes: The stand-in moves each position-actuated joint by a fixed placeholder fraction toward its control value from the model-default reset state; it has no seed input and its motion is not MuJoCo's physics.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it reads the pinned MJCF and its include for the ten hinge joints, the ten position actuators and their effective ctrlranges, but integrates a placeholder first-order motion of each actuated joint toward its control value; trajectories, contacts, actuator dynamics and the model's inertials are not MuJoCo's
the model's ten <position> actuators are position servos with kp and forcerange; the fake's first-order step is not a position servo and ignores kp, forcerange, damping, inertia and the joint ranges
the MJCF declares no <option timestep>, so the fake uses MuJoCo's library default 0.002 s as a placeholder; the reported 2.0 ms comes from the fake, not from a line of the clone
the fake has no mj_getState/mj_setState/mj_stateSize, so the bridge uses its basic checkpoint profile: time, qpos, qvel and ctrl are restored, not MuJoCo's full integration state
no mesh, texture, collision, contact or camera is loaded or resolved by the stand-in; the bridge exposes qpos, qvel, ctrl and time, not the SimpleEnv.grab_image frames
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so the stand-in was not compared with the real engine, and the example scenes were not loaded
the package serves the card's models[0], asset/robotis_omy/scene.xml, only, and no physical OMY arm is modelled or driven

the robot-and-floor scene omits the tabletop task objects, and bridge stepping combines a ten-control write with integration; SimpleEnv.step only stages targets and step_env integrates separately (mujoco_env/y_env.py:139-151)
the e-stop retains ctrl and the position targets; releasing the latch changes no integration state, and an explicit step with no action reuses the stored targets

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.
measures.name: native_checkpoint

safe_state.description: the bridge-owned simulation stops advancing: no step or world reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, while the integration state and stored ctrl stay readable; releasing the latch does not integrate or clear ctrl, and a new explicit step without an action reuses the stored position targets
